newsitem.title: HUNGARY: IEB 1996 SATISFACTORY, PLANS CAPITAL HIKE.
newsitem.headline: IEB 1996 SATISFACTORY, PLANS CAPITAL HIKE.

text.p: Hungary's Inter-Europa Bank Rt (IEB) said on Thursday that its results for this year would be satisfactory, though weaker than planned due to increasing competition.
IEB officials told a news conference that according to calculations the bank needed additional equity of some 1.5 billion forints, which may urge IEB to issue new shares next year.
The bank is part of Italy's San Paolo di Bancario group.
IEB general director Pierre Franco Rubatto told a news conference that Hungarian banks' liquidity had improved, but at the same time interest rate margins had diminished.
"Despite this, our balance sheet still shows very good figures,"0he said.

IEB said in a statement that corporate and personal deposits increased much quicker than expected, altogether by 12 billion forints between January and September, with deposits from the public accounting for almost half of the rise.
As a result, for the first time in the bank's history, client deposits covered the bank's loans, diminishing its depenedency on volatile interbank rates, IEB said in the statement.
IEB said earlier on Thursday that its pre-tax profit in the January-September perigd rose to 1.55 billion forints, from 1.36 billion in the corresponding period of 1995.
Rubatto said the pre-tax profit was likely to reach two billion forints by the end of the year, compared with the 2.25 billion forint target.
Tougher competition had compelled the bank to change its strategy in the second half of this year, he said.
The balance sheet total rose to 81.3 billion forints by September from 63.3 billion in January, compared with the target of 69.3 billion for the end of the year.

However, Rubatto said, the bank needed more capital on the increasingly competitive Hungarian market and the board of directors planned to ask permission from next year's annual shareholders' meeting for two capital increases.
In the first stage, IEB would double its registered capital from the profit reserves, by giving the shareholders one additional share on top of each share they had.

In the second step, the company would issue new shares, in an amount which would depend on the shareholders' decision about the dividend to be paid for 1996 and IEB's position on the banking market next year, Rubatto said.

IEB Chairman Laszlo Body said the bank did not plan to increase its balance sheet total substantially further this year, and the likely figure for the end of this year was between 80 and 85 billion forints.
